entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Mr. S.M. Abdullah P, learned counsel for the petitioners.

Also heard Mr.
R.J. Baruah, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the State.

2. This is an application made under Section 439 Cr.P.C., seeking bail by the petitioners, namely,
Ashad Ullah and Inamul Hoque, in connection with Moirabari P.S. Case No. 74/2024, registered under Section 120(B)/419/420/467/468/471/34 IPC r/w Section 66(C)/66(D) of I.T. Act.
3.

The background of the case is that on 15.05.2024 an FIR was lodged before the Officer-in-Charge of Moirabari police station, alleging inter alia that accused No. 1 has been running an illegal racket where he morphed the image of people from different locations across the country and fraudulently creates numerous identities in order to gain wrongful loans from different finance companies by using electronic devices such as mobile phone, computer/laptops and other fake documents as cyber crime.
During investigation, it came to know that the accused No. 1 along with other two co-accused has running this kind of illegal activities.

On being searched, one laptop, 13 numbers of mobile handsets, 15 numbers of debit cards, 20 numbers of jio sims, one aircel sim, 4 numbers of airtel sims, 33 numbers of Vodafone sims and 122 numbers of BSNL sims were recovered.
On the basis of the FIR a case was registered vide Moirabari P.S. case No. 74/2024.
Page No.# 3/4 4.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners are no way involved in the instant case.

It is also submitted that there is allegation against the FIR named accused Nos. 2 and 3 and the petitioners were arrested only on suspicion without any valid reasons and nothing was recovered from their possession.
It is also submitted that the petitioners have been detained in custody since 16.05.2024.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioners has further submitted that assuming not admitting the allegations made against the petitioners are true, then at best section 66(C)/66(D) of I.T. Act are applicable against the petitioners which are bailable in nature and other section of IPC is not applicable against them.
6.

The learned counsel has referred the case of Sharat Babu Digumarti vs. Government (NCT of Delhi) reported in (2017) 2 SCC 18, wherein it was observed that once the special provisions having the overriding effect to cover a criminal act and the offender, he gets out of the net of IPC.

entities.text: Sharat Babu Digumarti vs. Government (NCT of Delhi) reported in (2017) 2 SCC 18
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The electronic forms of transmission are covered by the I.T. Act, which is a special law.
It is a settled position of law that a special law shall prevail over the general and prior laws.
Accordingly to learned counsel, considering the background of the case as well as length of detention, the petitioners may be enlarged on bail.
7. On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor has produced the case diary and submits that there are sufficient incriminating materials found in the case diary against the petitioners.
The petitioners along with the other co-accused have involved in impersonating others by fabricating Pancard and Aadhaar Card.
Considering the gravity of the Page No.# 4/4 offence, bail may not be granted to the petitioners.

Page No.# 1/4 vs The State Of Assam on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49695928/
2 8.

On perusal of case diary, it reveals that the accused/petitioners and other co-accused for last couple of years, took huge amount of loan from various financial institutions by using fake Aadhaar card and PAN Card of different persons.
Investigation is on the initial stage.
9. In view of above, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the petitioners at this stage of investigation.
Accordingly, bail prayer of the petitioners is rejected.

10. The bail application stands disposed of accordingly.
11. Return the case diary.
